elements.quote: Followup endoscopy rates as an indicator of effectiveness in colon capsule endoscopy: a systematic review and meta- analysis.
elements.reason: The title explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review and meta-analysis.

elements.quote: Followup endoscopy rates as an indicator of effectiveness in colon capsule endoscopy: a systematic review and meta- analysis.
elements.reason: The title states the key focus and domain—follow-up endoscopy rates in the context of colon capsule endoscopy—indicating the review question and intervention/exposure.

elements.quote: a systematic review and meta- analysis.
elements.reason: The title includes the analysis method (systematic review and meta-analysis), which is relevant supplementary information.

elements.quote: Despite accumulating evidence of its diagnostic accuracy over the last decade, scepticism regarding its clinical effectiveness and cost- efficiency continues to hinder widespread acceptance.
elements.reason: Describes the current knowledge (diagnostic accuracy evidence) and key uncertainties (ongoing scepticism about clinical effectiveness and cost-efficiency).

elements.quote: This underscores the importance of understanding and optimising the FER for the successful integration of CCE into routine clinical practice. Despite its significance, a systematic review of FER in CCE remains absent.
elements.reason: Explains why the review is needed (FER affects implementation) and identifies a gap (no prior systematic review of FER in CCE).

elements.quote: A Chinese systematic review was identified during the abstract screening stage; however, none of its referenced studies met the inclusion criteria and were therefore excluded. 15
elements.reason: The authors identify and cite a previous systematic review, but they do not clearly position the current review as an update/replication or explicitly explain how it differs from or improves upon that prior review in the rationale.
The review evaluates follow-up endoscopy rates after a diagnostic test (CCE), not the effects of an intervention; a mechanism of action for an intervention is not applicable.
The review does not evaluate a complex intervention or implementation strategy requiring a logic model; it synthesizes outcomes of a diagnostic modality.

elements.quote: The primary aim of the review was to evaluate the FER following CCE. The secondary aims include exploring contributing factors to the FER to guide future research to reduce this rate further.
elements.reason: The review explicitly states primary and secondary aims, but the objectives are not framed using a question‑formulation framework (e.g., PICO/PEO).

The review does not evaluate intervention effects or planned comparisons; it synthesizes follow-up endoscopy rates after colon capsule endoscopy and factors influencing those rates (e.g., text_4 and text_5), so PICO comparisons are not applicable.

elements.quote: A systematic literature search conducted on 15 August 2024, yielded 3548 articles across three databases.
elements.reason: The last search date is reported for the database search, but no dates are provided for the manual reference list searching.

elements.quote: The literature search was conducted across EMBASE, MEDLINE, and PubMed databases... The electronic search covered studies published between January 2004 and August 2024
elements.reason: Database names and an overall coverage period are reported, but the search interface/platform (e.g., Ovid, Embase.com) is not specified.
No study registers, regulatory databases, or online repositories were reported as searched.
No websites, search engines, or other online sources beyond bibliographic databases and reference lists were reported as searched.
No organisations or manufacturers were reported as contacted.
No individuals were reported as contacted to identify studies.

elements.quote: Additional studies were identified through manual searches of reference lists from the selected publications.
elements.reason: Specifies that reference lists of selected publications were examined.
Backward citation searching (manual reference list searches) was performed, but seed reports, citation index/platform, and search dates were not reported.
Journals or conference proceedings were not reported as directly consulted; conference abstracts were excluded.

elements.quote: Titles and abstracts of all retrieved studies were independently screened by pairs of authors, with each set assigned to one of the following pairs: IIL and AR or AA and CT.
elements.reason: Reports two reviewers (pairs) for title/abstract screening, but does not clearly state how many reviewers screened full-text reports.

elements.quote: Titles and abstracts of all retrieved studies were independently screened by pairs of authors
elements.reason: Independence is stated for title/abstract screening; independence at full-text screening is not explicitly reported.

elements.quote: Discrepancies within each group were resolved through discussion among the respective reviewers.
elements.reason: Provides a clear process (discussion among reviewers) to resolve screening disagreements.
No description of contacting study investigators to obtain or confirm eligibility information was found.
Although no language restrictions were stated, the methods used to translate abstracts or articles for eligibility assessment were not described.
No details are provided about the use or integration of automation tools in study selection.
No use of externally derived classifiers is identified or described.
No internally derived classifiers or their training/validation are described.
No machine-learning prioritisation tools or stopping/prioritisation rules are described.
No crowdsourcing platforms or their integration into study selection are reported.
No use of previously screened datasets to eliminate records is described.

elements.quote: data extraction was performed by I.L.
elements.reason: Explicitly states that one reviewer (I.L.) performed data extraction, thereby reporting the number of data extractors.
No statement indicates whether multiple data collectors worked independently during data extraction.
No process is described for resolving disagreements between data collectors for data extraction.
No processes for obtaining or confirming data from study investigators are reported.
No automation tools for data collection are described.
Although the authors state there were no language restrictions and non-English articles would be translated if eligible, no methods for translation used during data collection are reported.
No software for extracting data from figures is specified.
No decision rules are described for selecting data from multiple reports or resolving inconsistencies.

elements.quote: The primary aim of the review was to evaluate the FER following CCE. The secondary aims include exploring contributing factors to the FER to guide future research to reduce this rate further. The FER refers to additional urgent colonoscopy or flexible sigmoidoscopy required after initial CCE due to incomplete procedures, inadequate bowel preparation, or the need for therapeutic interventions or histological biopsies.
elements.reason: Explicitly lists the outcome domain (FER) and provides a clear definition of how FER is determined.
No time frame of measurement for FER (e.g., follow-up window after CCE) is specified in the provided text.
The manuscript does not state whether all compatible results within the FER outcome domain (e.g., across measures, time points, analyses) were sought.
No description is provided of any process for selecting among multiple compatible results within the FER domain.
No report of changes to outcome inclusion, definitions, or importance and no rationale for such changes are provided.
No report of changes to processes for selecting results within the FER outcome domain is provided.

elements.quote: The primary aim of the review was to evaluate the FER following CCE.
elements.reason: Identifies the most important outcome (primary outcome: FER) but does not provide a rationale for prioritizing this outcome.

elements.quote: The extracted details included the CCE indication, patient selection criteria, sex, mean age, FER, the type of investigation modality, ... capsule type, bowel preparation regimen (including prokinetic drugs and boosters), study design, sample size, bowel cleansing quality and CCE complete transit rate (see online supplemental tables A2 and A3).
elements.reason: The manuscript lists multiple variables for which data were sought, but these variables are not defined in the provided text (definitions are not given for most items).
No description was found of assumptions made about missing or unclear study information.

elements.quote: The final selection of studies was reviewed, and data extraction was performed by I.L. The extracted details included...
elements.reason: No tool or framework is described or cited as being used to determine which data items to collect; therefore this conditional requirement does not apply.

elements.quote: All pooled estimates were calculated from the patient data of included studies using Freeman- Tukey double arcsine transformation... The meta- analysis used the 'meta' R package, specifically employing the 'metaprop' function, which calculates study- level effect sizes based on raw proportions.
elements.reason: Specifies the effect measure for the outcome (FER) as raw proportions, with pooling using the Freeman–Tukey transformation.

elements.quote: Compared with the key performance indicators for FERs in colonoscopy (0.10-0.15) and CT colonography (0.25), the pooled FER for CCE was found to be 0.42 (95% CI 0.34 to 0.50).
elements.reason: Provides threshold ranges used for interpretation (KPIs for other modalities), but does not explain the rationale for these thresholds beyond stating they are KPIs.
No re-expression of synthesized results into another effect measure is described; results are presented as proportions (with variance-stabilizing transformation) only.

elements.quote: All pooled estimates were calculated from the patient data of included studies using Freeman- Tukey double arcsine transformation, which stabilises variances in proportion data for reliable pooling.
elements.reason: Justifies the analytical choice by explaining that the Freeman–Tukey transformation was used to stabilize variances for proportion data.

elements.quote: The FER did not need to be explicitly stated as the study's primary or secondary endpoint but could be calculated from the available raw data. Exclusion criteria primarily focused on studies where follow- up investigations were conducted for upper GI findings, as these conditions would not typically be identified during colonoscopy, the gold standard for comparison of CCE FERs. Additionally, studies where all participants underwent both colonoscopy and CCE as part of a diagnostic accuracy study were excluded (see figure 1).
elements.reason: The authors describe how studies were deemed eligible for the synthesis based on having FER data (or data from which FER could be calculated) and list key exclusions. However, they do not clearly describe processes for allocating studies to each planned synthesis/subgroup (e.g., tabulating characteristics and matching to specific syntheses), so the description is incomplete.

elements.quote: All pooled estimates were calculated from the patient data of included studies using Freeman- Tukey double arcsine transformation, which stabilises variances in proportion data for reliable pooling. The meta- analysis used the 'meta' R package, specifically employing the 'metaprop' function, which calculates study- level effect sizes based on raw proportions.
elements.reason: They describe data preparation via a variance-stabilizing transformation and calculation of study-level proportions for pooling. However, no methods for handling missing summary statistics or other data-preparation steps (e.g., imputations/conversions for missing data) are reported.

elements.quote: Sensitivity analysis included a 'leave- one- out' approach, where each study was sequentially removed to assess its impact on the overall results. Additionally, studies with a high risk of bias were excluded to evaluate their influence on pooled estimates.
elements.reason: Methods explicitly describe two sensitivity analyses (leave-one-out and exclusion of high-risk-of-bias studies), providing details of the approaches used to assess robustness.
The manuscript reports conducting sensitivity analyses but does not indicate whether these analyses were pre-specified or post hoc.

elements.quote: Meta- regression, sensitivity analysis and publication bias assessment (Egger's test) were conducted using the 'metafor' R package.
elements.reason: Explicitly states the method used to assess reporting bias (Egger’s test), fulfilling the requirement to describe methods for assessing risk of bias due to missing results.
No multi-domain reporting-bias assessment tool was used; only Egger’s test/funnel plot are mentioned, so there are no domains/items or overall judgement process to report.
No existing reporting-bias tool was adapted; only Egger’s test was used.
No newly developed reporting-bias tool is described.
The manuscript does not report how many reviewers assessed reporting bias, their independence, or how disagreements were resolved.
No processes to obtain or confirm information from study investigators for reporting-bias assessment are described or implied.
No automation tool for reporting-bias assessment was used; only the 'metafor' R package for Egger’s test is mentioned, which is standard statistical software.

No method for assessing certainty/confidence in the body of evidence (e.g., GRADE) is described anywhere in the retrieved Methods or related sections; only risk of bias (ROBINS-E) and statistical analyses are reported.
The manuscript does not report factors or criteria used to judge certainty/confidence in the evidence.
No decision rules or levels for deriving an overall certainty/confidence rating are provided.
No certainty/confidence assessment was conducted; therefore, review-specific certainty considerations or thresholds do not apply.
No certainty/confidence assessment system was used, so no adaptations can be reported.
The number of reviewers, independence, and procedures for resolving disagreements for certainty/confidence assessment are not reported.
No certainty/confidence assessment was performed; no processes to obtain or confirm information from investigators for this purpose are described.
No automation tools for certainty/confidence assessment are reported.
Methods for reporting certainty/confidence results (e.g., Summary of Findings tables) are not described.
No standard certainty/confidence phrases or guidance sources are reported because no certainty assessment was undertaken.

The manuscript provides only aggregate reasons for exclusion (e.g., via the PRISMA flow diagram and narrative counts) but does not cite individual studies that were excluded after full-text review nor give the specific reason for each excluded study.

elements.quote: one study identified through hand- searching was included, resulting in a total of 19 studies 1 2 16-32 with 2850 participants included in the meta- analysis.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly cites the set of included studies by their reference numbers (1, 2, and 16–32), indicating every included study is cited.

elements.quote: The extracted details included the CCE indication, patient selection criteria, sex, mean age, FER, the type of investigation modality, ... bowel cleansing quality and CCE complete transit rate (see online supplemental tables A2 and A3).
elements.reason: The text indicates key study characteristics are tabulated in online supplemental tables A2 and A3, supporting comparison. However, the provided evidence does not show the tables themselves or explicitly confirm that characteristics are presented for every included study.

elements.quote: The studies included in this analysis underwent a risk of bias assessment utilising the Risk of Bias In Nonrandomized Studies of Exposure (ROBIN- E) tool across seven domains due to mixed included study types.
elements.reason: This is not an intervention review; included studies are nonrandomized/observational. Therefore, an additional table of intervention details is not applicable.

elements.quote: The studies included in this analysis underwent a risk of bias assessment utilising the Risk of Bias In Nonrandomized Studies of Exposure (ROBIN- E) tool across seven domains due to mixed included study types. 10 The risk of bias for each domain was classified as low, moderate, critical, or no information available. Studies receiving a critical risk rating in any domain were considered to have a high risk of bias (see online supplemental table A4).
elements.reason: They report domain-level assessments using ROBINS-E and refer to a supplemental table, implying tabulated results. However, the retrieved content does not show per-study domain-level and overall judgments, so full presentation for every included study cannot be verified.
No justifications for each individual risk-of-bias judgment are presented in the retrieved content; only general comments about common sources of bias are provided elsewhere.
The retrieved results do not display outcome-specific risk-of-bias judgments alongside study results (e.g., in the forest plot or result tables).

elements.quote: The two high- risk studies were included in a sensitivity analysis to assess their impact on the overall findings (see online supplemental figure A4). ... The sensitivity analysis using both leave- one- out analysis and filtered out the two high- risk studies showed consistent effect size estimates across all iterations. No single study disproportionately influenced the overall results (see online supplemental figures A2 and A3)
elements.reason: Results are reported for both pre-specified sensitivity analyses: leave-one-out and exclusion of high-risk studies, stating their impacts.

elements.quote: The sensitivity analysis using both leave- one- out analysis and filtered out the two high- risk studies showed consistent effect size estimates across all iterations. No single study disproportionately influenced the overall results ... demonstrating the robustness of the meta- analysis.
elements.reason: The authors explicitly interpret the sensitivity analyses as showing consistent estimates and conclude that the meta-analysis is robust.
No evidence of tables comparing original versus sensitivity-analysis results, assumptions, and contributing studies was found in the retrieved text.
Sensitivity-analysis results are not shown in forest plots in the retrieved evidence; forest plots presented relate to subgroup analyses, not sensitivity analyses.

No assessment of overall certainty/confidence in the body of evidence for any outcome is reported in the retrieved Results; only pooled estimates, heterogeneity, publication bias testing, and risk-of-bias at study level are presented.
No reasons for rating certainty up or down (e.g., across GRADE domains) are provided in the retrieved evidence.
Certainty of evidence is not communicated alongside results in any Results subsection or figures within the retrieved content.

No Summary of Findings or other evidence summary tables reporting certainty are mentioned in the retrieved text; only supplemental tables for data extraction, risk of bias, and meta-regression are referenced.

elements.quote: The pooled FER in our study was 42%, which appears relatively high when compared with benchmarks in related procedures like colonoscopy and CTC. ... In the context of CTC, cost- effectiveness is significantly reduced when FERs exceed 30% (16). The Royal College of Radiologists in the UK recommends a reinvestigation threshold of <25% as a KPI. 42 When compared with these benchmarks, the 42% FER in our study underscores the need for targeted strategies to mitigate factors contributing to this high rate.
elements.reason: The Discussion interprets the study’s pooled FER by directly comparing it with benchmarks and guidelines from related procedures (colonoscopy and CT colonography), situating the findings within existing evidence.

elements.quote: Finally, this study has several limitations. The first is the high heterogeneity in the results. Despite applying meta- regression and subgroup analysis, heterogeneity remained substantial. This was primarily driven by multiple confounding variables within each covariate, including the lack of a standardised bowel preparation and booster regimen, variability in CCE indications, differing exclusion criteria, and inconsistencies in national referral thresholds due to variations in guidelines, such as the NHS England CCE guidance 68 69 and ESGE 2012 guideline 70 (see online supplemental tables A2-A4 and A6). ... In addition, CCE indications were not consistently documented across all included studies, and subgrouping them during the meta- analysis process may have introduced bias. Furthermore, the limited number of studies, particularly within subgroup analyses, may have reduced statistical power, preventing definitive conclusions.
elements.reason: The Discussion explicitly identifies limitations of the included evidence such as substantial heterogeneity due to varying protocols and indications, inconsistent documentation across studies, and a limited number of studies affecting statistical power.

elements.quote: CCE indications were not consistently documented across all included studies, and subgrouping them during the meta- analysis process may have introduced bias.
elements.reason: The authors explicitly acknowledge a limitation stemming from their review process (the subgrouping approach used during synthesis), noting it may have introduced bias.

elements.quote: CCE indications were not consistently documented across all included studies, and subgrouping them during the meta- analysis process may have introduced bias. Furthermore, the limited number of studies, particularly within subgroup analyses, may have reduced statistical power, preventing definitive conclusions.
elements.reason: They indicate that their subgrouping approach could introduce bias and that the small number of studies reduced statistical power, hindering definitive conclusions. However, the specific impact of the subgrouping-related bias on results (e.g., direction or magnitude) is not elaborated, nor are other process limitations (e.g., search restrictions) discussed for impact.

elements.quote: ⇒ Refining CCE indications, improving completion rates and bowel preparation, and optimising patient selection could reduce unnecessary follow- up procedures... These improvements could enhance cost- effectiveness and increase patient satisfaction by minimising invasive testing and streamlining the diagnostic pathway.
elements.reason: Directly outlines practice implications, including strategies to reduce follow-up procedures and improve patient pathways and satisfaction.

elements.quote: This prioritisation role of CCE could be crucial in CRC screening programmes, reducing the number of patients on waiting lists and shortening colonoscopy wait times, particularly in an already strained healthcare system.
elements.reason: Discusses implications for health system planning and screening programmes, which are policy-level considerations.

elements.quote: Future research should focus on improving completion rates, bowel preparation protocols, and refining CCE indications.
elements.reason: Provides explicit recommendations for future research priorities.

elements.quote: This study protocol was designed following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and MetaAnalyses (PRISMA) guidelines (PRISMA checklist in the online supplemental file) 9 and is registered with the PROSPERO International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (registration number: CRD42024567959).
elements.reason: The manuscript reports the register name (PROSPERO) and provides the registration number (CRD42024567959).

elements.quote: This study protocol was designed following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and MetaAnalyses (PRISMA) guidelines (PRISMA checklist in the online supplemental file) 9 and is registered with the PROSPERO International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (registration number: CRD42024567959).
elements.reason: The authors indicate the protocol’s registration in PROSPERO and provide the registration number, specifying where the protocol can be accessed.
The manuscript notes PROSPERO registration (CRD42024567959) but does not describe any amendments to the registration or protocol.
No reasons for amendments are reported; amendments are not mentioned anywhere in the retrieved text.
The stage at which any amendments were implemented is not reported; no amendments are described.
